topics.topic: Replay ordering between concurrent creates sharing a request ID and an intervening erasure
questions: May an erasure be ordered between two already-concurrent creates carrying the same request id, making the second a new create, or must both creates be resolved as repeat/refusal before that erasure can apply?

quotes: Creates of one model carrying one request id are applied one at a time: of two concurrent ones, the first makes the record and the second is a repeat or refused by rule 4 or 5.

A create and the anonymisation or erasure that removes its request id are applied one at a time too, each on the result of the one before: a repeat applied before it answers the record as rule 4 says, one applied after it is a new create (rule 8).
judgement.why: The first passage requires the second concurrent create to be a repeat or refusal, while the second permits an intervening erasure to make that same create a new create.

bases.passage: Creates of one model carrying one request id are applied one at a time: of two concurrent ones, the first makes the record and the second is a repeat or refused by rule 4 or 5.
bases.rests_on: A create repeated after a lost answer — with or without a caller-supplied id — never silently makes a second project, customer or room, and never damages one.

bases.passage: A create and the anonymisation or erasure that removes its request id are applied one at a time too, each on the result of the one before: a repeat applied before it answers the record as rule 4 says, one applied after it is a new create (rule 8).
bases.rests_on: Erasing a customer or anonymising a project removes everything that would tell a repeat (R0-06, R0-62); a create repeated after that is a new create, checked as any create, and when accepted its answer shows the new record it made.

witness.initial: No Customer carries request id K; the owner has a valid owner session and valid Customer facts F.
events: The owner concurrently submits two 'record a customer' calls C1 and C2 with request id K and facts F.
C1 commits and creates Customer X.
The owner submits and confirms erasure of Customer X while C2 remains pending.
Registry applies either C2 or the erasure next.
outcomes: Under the concurrent-creates passage, C2 is applied as a repeat and answers Customer X; the erasure then erases X, and no Customer Y is created.
Under the create-versus-erasure passage, the erasure may remove X's request id before C2 is applied; C2 is then a new create and creates Customer Y.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether C2 answers Customer X or creates Customer Y; the stored Customers and audit entries also differ.
basis: 'Create a project', 'record a customer', 'add a room' and 'publish an artifact pointer' each carry a request id: an opaque value the caller makes, unique for every create it means as new — printable text of at most 128 characters, made from at least 16 random bytes, as a random UUID is; a blank one is missing (A02).

| record a customer | owner | the Customer with the identity (`customer_ref`) Registry minted for it (R0-16), its kind — person or company — its contact data (R0-06, R0-37) and, when given, its fiscal data: tax id (NIF/NIE/CIF) and legal name (R0-80) | missing name or kind refused; recording the same person again makes a second Customer (R0-16) |

| erase a customer's contact data | owner | the Customer keeps only its identity and the fact that it was erased; name, phone, e-mail and language are gone; projects still name it (R0-06) | unknown customer refused; erasing an erased customer returns it unchanged |

A create and the anonymisation or erasure that removes its request id are applied one at a time too, each on the result of the one before: a repeat applied before it answers the record as rule 4 says, one applied after it is a new create (rule 8).
